mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates applied to future cash flows reduce the present value of expected corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative after the trigger (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS increase is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) coinciding with a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests strengthening labor demand, which elevates corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while UNRATE falls by >0.5% over the next month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60 days after trigger, or UNRATE increase offsets PAYEMS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in HOUST (residential construction) above 2% for two consecutive months predicts increased future economic momentum, resulting in positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive over the 2-month high-HOUST window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 5% signals supply-side weakness, which reduces earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by <5% over the same horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) exceeds 233 for three consecutive months, it indicates persistent inflation pressure, prompting the Fed to maintain higher rates and suppressing equity discount rates, which drives negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not statistically different from zero after the CPI threshold is breached.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 6% followed by a sustained rise to 5.5% within a month signals labor market cooling, reducing growth expectations and resulting in negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 6% and then rises to <5.5% in the following month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative after the UNRATE pattern occurs.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both GDPC1 (GDP) and PAYEMS (labor) above their 2023 Q4 averages for the next 20 days is associated with elevated earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive return when both proxies are above their 2023 Q4 averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS (retail sales) by more than 15% in a single month, combined with a decline in INDPRO, predicts supply-side weakness that dampens earnings growth and produces negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >15% while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative after the combined drop occurs.
